title: Proper flat perfect direct image in independently supplied derived models
statement: Let f:X→Y be a proper, flat, locally finitely presented morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Supply derived categories of module sheaves on X and Y with possibly different Hom universes, and derived categories on their respective localized open sites [def-pc-derived-category]. For every perfect object E of D(O_X) [def-pc-perfect-complex], the shared derived direct image Rf_*E [def-pc-derived-direct-image] is perfect on Y. Neither quasi-compactness of Y nor a right adjoint is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 36.30.4(1), Tag 0B91 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B91), its proof using Lemma 36.30.1, Tag 0A1H

proof.text: Represent E as QK using essential surjectivity of DerivedCategory.Q and transport perfectness along QK ≅ E. For every point retain the same open U and strictly perfect complex L. mapDerivedCategoryFactors identifies each restricted QK with Q of the termwise restricted K. Localization.uniq and compUniqFunctor transfer the isomorphism to QL to the standard localization on U. Thus K remains perfect in the standard source and open models in Hom universe u+1; all standard scheme and open models are constructed by HasDerivedCategory.standard.

Apply properSupport_perfect_directImage to QK and the actual single complex G = O_X[0]. Its bounds are [0,0]. O_X is invertible and finitely presented, and the zero terms are finitely presented because a rank-zero free module is zero. isFlatOver_of_isInvertible gives relative flatness of the degree-zero term; for other degrees the section modules are subsingleton and hence flat. finite_type_module_support_closed gives closed term supports. Each reduced closed support immersion followed by the proper f is proper. Properness also supplies quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. The first conclusion is perfectness of Rf_*(QK tensor QG). singleFunctorIsoCompQ identifies QG with the derived tensor unit; tensorIso followed by rightUnitor identifies QK tensor QG with QK. Transport the local strictly perfect witnesses along the direct image of this isomorphism.

Set J = f_*I(K), using the existing functorial K-injective resolution, independent of the supplied derived localizations. derivedModuleDirectImageFactorization represents the standard direct image of QK as QJ. Transfer perfectness of QJ to the supplied target localization and the supplied localizations on its opens by the first-step exact-restriction and localization-uniqueness argument. The same factorization in the original source and target models, composed with the direct image of QK ≅ E, gives Rf_*E ≅ QJ. Transfer perfectness back along that isomorphism. All transports are proved private helpers, and no sorry is added.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0B91(1), proof invoking Tag 0A1H; sources read online 2026-10-13. S1 Lean proof uses Mathlib localization uniqueness and the shared K-injective direct-image factorization to implement the independent-Hom-universe transport.

lean.statement:
theorem properFlat_derivedDirectImage_perfect
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsProper f] [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wY} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    [∀ U : Y.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{wY} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory X) (hE : Scheme.IsPerfect X E) :
    Scheme.IsPerfect Y ((schemeDerivedDirectImage f).obj E)
